clue.text: Punch clock

definitions.meaning: to punch someone is to hit them, to deliver a blow
informally, to clock someone is to hit them, as in clocked him on the jaw

explanation.definitionFit: Both clue words are verbs for landing a blow on someone, and the answer is the general verb for hitting.

clue.text: A tall nurse treated film comedian

indicators.note: treated as in processed or worked on, so the letters of the three words are reworked

explanation.surface: A tall nurse gives care to a famous screen comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges ATALLNURSE into the comedian's name.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the thin half of the classic comedy double act with Oliver Hardy, a film comedian.

clue.text: Picture of forged coin

indicators.note: forged means faked or hammered into new shape, so the letters of the word are remade

explanation.surface: An image of a counterfeit piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a picture, especially a religious image painted on wood.

clue.text: On reflection, partaking in absinthe endures

indicators.note: the answer takes part in the run of letters across the two words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, someone who drinks absinthe keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partaking in' signals letters found inside 'absinthe endures'; 'On reflection' is not a reversal signal here but the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean after all things are considered, as a final judgement.

clue.text: First chess player attending match in formal evening dress

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so one piece stands beside the other

parts.note: the side with the white pieces always moves first in chess
a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: The opening player at a chess match is dressed formally.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the most formal style of evening wear, a tailcoat with a white bow tie.

clue.text: Deliver diamonds in German city

indicators.note: in places the card suit letter inside the name of the city

parts.note: Hanover is a city in Lower Saxony, Germany
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: Delivering jewels in a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over something is to deliver or surrender it to someone else.

clue.text: Coppers stride off in a display of team spirit

indicators.note: off as in gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police officers march away together, showing their loyalty to the unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges COPPERSSTRIDE; 'in a display of' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means the shared pride and loyalty of a group, its team spirit.

clue.text: Ape straddling an awning

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: A monkey sits astride a shop's sunshade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' is a verb here, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering of cloth, much like an awning.

clue.text: Stake boat

definitions.meaning: a bet or wager, a stake placed on something
a flat-bottomed boat pushed along with a pole, common on rivers at Oxford and Cambridge

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a gamble in betting slang and a flat river craft propelled by a pole.

clue.text: Soldier who carries the Colours in — gen's misleading

indicators.note: misleading as in leading astray, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is counted as a letter here

explanation.surface: A general's account of the regimental standard-bearer is deceptive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misleading' rearranges INGENS; the dash only links.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British army the most junior infantry officer once carried the regimental flag, called an ensign.

clue.text: Liking page with charm

parts.note: to enchant someone is to charm or delight them

explanation.surface: Fondness for a pageboy who has charisma.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or fondness for something.

clue.text: Fail to win card game — become exasperated

parts.note: to fail to win a game is to lose it
patience is the British name for solitaire, a card game for one

explanation.surface: Losing at cards makes someone irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to run out of tolerance and grow annoyed.

clue.text: Scratched one?

parts.note: a horse scratched from a race is withdrawn and so never starts it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratched' suggests something itchy or marked, but in racing a scratched entrant is withdrawn before the off.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner pulled out of a race fails to begin it; the word also means any idea with no chance of success.

clue.text: Trying more ties out

indicators.note: out as in disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trying on more neckties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MORETIES; 'Trying' is an adjective here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trying taxes your patience, which is what tedious or wearisome means.

clue.text: Bridge player held in low esteem

indicators.note: held in means contained within the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A card player at bridge is not thought much of.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The four seats at a bridge table are named North, South, East and the remaining compass point.

clue.text: Changing of editor, highly desirable

indicators.note: changing the letters means rearranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: A change of editor would be most welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges OFEDITOR, so 'of' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something so wonderful one would give anything for it.

clue.text: Element causing trouble amongst our sailors

indicators.note: amongst places one piece between the two letters of the other

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's own sailors
ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: Something is stirring up bother among the crew of our navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive noble gas, number 86 in the periodic table, so a chemical element.

clue.text: Stage one in unhappy retirement

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the turned word
retirement means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: unhappy means sad
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A phase of life spent miserably after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns SAD into DAS, and 'in' puts I inside to give D-A-I-S.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform in a hall, a small stage.

clue.text: Frail head going round food shop

parts.note: frail means delicate

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A weak leader making a tour of a grocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a leader, but it is a headland; 'going round' reverses that word, which follows the synonym for 'Frail'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling prepared meats, cheeses and fine foods is a delicatessen.

clue.text: Tender doctor returned wearing costume

indicators.note: something wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes, a costume

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A gentle physician comes back dressed in fancy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like gentle, but it is the verb meaning to offer; 'returned' reverses the doctor's letters and 'wearing' puts them inside the costume word.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something, such as a resignation, is to submit or offer it.

clue.text: I attempt to arrest a villainous character

parts.note: taken as written
a go is an attempt, as in have a go

explanation.surface: Someone tries to apprehend a wicked man.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheming ensign in Shakespeare's Othello is a famous stage villain.

clue.text: Colour of object surrounded by seaweed

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: laver is an edible seaweed, used in Welsh laverbread
an end is an object or aim, as in to that end

explanation.surface: Something found wrapped in kelp is coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple shade named after the flower is a colour.

clue.text: Tax office

definitions.meaning: a levy on goods, such as customs or excise
an obligation or task that falls to someone, as in the office of a host

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a government charge on imports and a moral obligation or function.

clue.text: Novel from library, or borrowed? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary means the other way round, so the letters run backwards
from shows that the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A book from the library, or was it borrowed? The other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are taken from 'library, or borrowed' and then 'On the contrary' runs them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Scott's 1817 novel is named after the Scottish outlaw.

clue.text: Policeman determined to avoid responsibility

parts.note: a cop is a policeman
out to do something means determined to do it, as in out to win

explanation.surface: An officer is set on dodging blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'determined to' gives OUT because 'out to' means set on; 'to' then joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop out is a colloquial verb for evading a duty or commitment.

clue.text: Sample mushrooms brought back by me after breaking in

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ceps are edible mushrooms, also called porcini

indicators.note: breaking into a word puts something inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sample of mushrooms that I brought home after a break-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns CEPS into SPEC; then ME breaks IN to make I-ME-N.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is an example or sample taken for study.
